sections.h2: What does an Iowa quitclaim deed actually transfer?
sections.html:
It transfers whatever interest the person signing holds, and nothing more is promised. Under Iowa Code 558.19, the sample quitclaim form states a consideration in dollars and says the grantor quitclaims to the grantee all interest in a described tract.

The statute offers other sample forms for comparison. The fee simple deed without warranty uses the words "hereby convey," and the warranty deed adds a warranty of title against all persons. Each form is called sufficient if varied to suit the circumstances, so the quitclaim is a legally valid choice. The difference is the promise the grantor makes.

That is why a quitclaim fits transfers between people who already know the property's history, such as adding a spouse or moving a house into a family arrangement. It fits less well when a stranger is paying money and expects a promise about title.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a quitclaim deed in an Iowa county?
sections.html:
Recording usually costs $5 per page plus two $1 charges, and transfer tax may add to that if money changed hands. The recorder's schedule comes from Iowa Code 331.604.

ChargeAmountSource
Recording, real estate instrument$5 per page or fraction, per transaction331.604
Records management fund$1 per recorded transaction331.604
Electronic transaction fund$1 per recorded transaction331.604
Transfer tax80 cents per $500 or fraction over the first $500 of consideration428A.1
Groundwater hazard statementNo recorder fee558.69

Counties may add services or rules of their own, so call the recorder before you mail a deed.

sections.h2: How should an Iowa quitclaim deed be formatted for the recorder?
sections.html:
Each recorder sets format requirements, and one county's published list is a good guide. The Story County Recorder asks for the following on deeds:

  • A minimum of three inches of blank space at the top of the first page.
  • The preparer's name, address and phone number typed directly below that space.
  • The line "Address Tax Statement To" with the taxpayer's name and address, directly under the preparer information.
  • A full legal description. The shortened description on a tax statement should not be used.
  • Printed names beneath every signature, including the acknowledging officer.
  • A signed, dated and notarized document that is legible and reproducible.

Other counties may differ in small ways. You can see the Story County recording requirements for the full list.

sections.h2: Who must notarize an Iowa deed, and can it be done remotely?
sections.html:
A deed must be acknowledged before a notarial officer before it can be lawfully recorded (558.42), and the acknowledgment must follow Chapter 9B (558.20). The signer declares before the officer that the signature is theirs and given for the stated purpose, and an entity signer must have authority.

Under Chapter 9B, the officer must confirm identity through personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence. Accepted evidence includes a passport, driver's license or government nondriver ID that is current or expired no more than three years, or a credible witness. The officer may refuse if not satisfied that the signer has capacity or signs knowingly and voluntarily.

Remote notarization is allowed under 9B.14A. The notary and signer must communicate by sight and sound, identity needs personal knowledge, a credible witness or two types of identity proofing, and the notary must make and keep an audio-visual recording for at least ten years. The certificate must state that technology was used. Check with the recorder that the county accepts the resulting document.

sections.h2: When does a quitclaim deed owe Iowa transfer tax?
sections.html:
Transfer tax applies only when there is consideration above $500. The tax is 80 cents for each $500 or fraction over $500, and the person who conveys the property is liable (428A.1 and 428A.3).

Many family and court-driven transfers are exempt under 428A.2. The ones most relevant to quitclaims include:

  • Deeds between spouses, or between parent and child, without actual consideration. Cancelling debt secured by the property is not actual consideration if it does not exceed the property's fair market value.
  • Deeds between former spouses under a dissolution decree.
  • Deeds that correct, confirm or supplement a recorded deed without added consideration.
  • Deeds returning property to lienholders in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Deeds distributing trust assets to beneficiaries without consideration.

A recorder will not record an exempt deed without a signed statement claiming the exemption, filed with the deed or endorsed on it (428A.4). Knowingly failing to pay due tax, or willfully entering false information on a declaration of value, is a simple misdemeanor (428A.10 and 428A.15).

sections.h2: What is the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement?
sections.html:
Both are forms that go in with a deed. The declaration of value states the full consideration, must be signed by at least one seller or buyer or an agent, and is required unless the instrument falls in an exempt category. The recorder does not record it. The data goes to the assessor (428A.1).

The groundwater hazard statement under 558.69 covers known burial sites, wells, solid waste disposal sites, underground storage tanks, hazardous waste and private sewage systems. The owner is responsible for accuracy. If no such conditions exist, the first page of the deed must carry the exemption statement. A recorder must refuse the deed if the required statement is missing, although a recording made without it does not void the deed.

Story County's page notes that the groundwater process changed on July 1, 2022 under House File 2343, so use the current form from the recorder.

sections.h2: Does a spouse have to sign an Iowa quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Often yes. If the owner is married, a conveyance of the homestead is not valid unless the other spouse signs the same or a like instrument, or a power of attorney for it (561.13).

A spouse who holds only homestead rights and a statutory share may relinquish those rights specifically under 597.5 without joining the granting clause. The requirement does not apply if a dissolution decree ended the interest, if the right of recovery is barred under 614.15, for a purchase-money mortgage, or where a court of equity finds that invalidating the transaction would unjustly enrich the other spouse.

The homestead is the owner's home and the contiguous land used with it. Inside a city plat it is limited to one half acre, and outside a plat to forty acres (561.1 and 561.2).

sections.h2: When should a quitclaim deed not be the tool for selling an Iowa house?
sections.html:
An unrecorded instrument is invalid against later good-faith purchasers for value without notice, so recording the deed promptly protects the new owner (558.41). Transfers by quitclaim deed are also excluded from the seller disclosure requirement, which is one reason families use them between relatives.

Other recording rules can apply by property type. Entity transfers carry implied warranties unless the instrument says otherwise, including that the entity exists and the signer is authorized (558.72). Agricultural land conveyances must be recorded by the grantee within 180 days (558.44).

If the plan is to sell, ask the buyer or title company which form they want before you sign anything. Owners with liens, back taxes or unclear co-owners often need advice before deciding.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed legal in Iowa?
faqs.a: Yes. Iowa Code 558.19 lists the quitclaim form with fee simple deeds without warranty and with warranty as sufficient forms of conveyance.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record an Iowa quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Recording is $5 per page or fraction, plus $1 for the records management fund and $1 for the electronic transaction fund per recorded transaction. Transfer tax applies only if consideration exceeds $500.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need to be notarized in Iowa?
faqs.a: Yes. A deed must be acknowledged under Chapter 9B before it can be lawfully recorded, and remote notarization is allowed if the statutory conditions are met.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed remove my spouse's homestead rights?
faqs.a: Not by itself. A married owner's homestead conveyance is invalid without the spouse's signature on the same or a like instrument, with limited exceptions.

faqs.q: Can I quitclaim my house to my child without paying transfer tax in Iowa?
faqs.a: A deed between parent and child without actual consideration is exempt under 428A.2, but the exemption must be claimed in a signed statement and you may still owe recording fees.
